decisions.quote:
Group differences in OXT methylation between patients with Major Depressive Disorder and healthy controls: A pre-registered replication study
Simon Sanwald, Christian Montag, Markus Kiefer

ABSTRACT
Depression is linked to stress which leaves traces in the epigenetic signature of genes. The oxytocin system is implicated in allostatic processes promoting adaption to environmental stressors. Interactions of the oxytocin system with the environment, e.g., methylation of the gene coding for oxytocin (OXT), are candidates for the investigation of the biological underpinnings of depression. Recently, we found hypomethylation of OXT in patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) compared to healthy controls (HC). Since the replicability of findings is a key point of criticism in (epi‑)genetic research, we aimed to confirm our previous findings in a pre-registered study (data was stored in a database prior to pre-registration) within a new sample of n = 85 patients with MDD and n = 85 HC. We investigated OXT DNA-methylation in peripheral blood samples, stressful life events and depression
decisions.reason: The 2024 abstract (n = 85 MDD, n = 85 HC) retests and confirms "our previous findings" / "our previous study" showing OXT hypomethylation in MDD patients compared to healthy controls, alongside stressful life events (SLEs) and depression severity. In the complete deposited bibliography (bib0001-bib0058), bib0043 (10.1186/s12888-021-03166-6) studies SLC6A4, leaving two 2020 Sanwald et al. OXT methylation papers: bib0042 (J. Affect. Disord., 10.1016/j.jad.2020.07.068, shipped row 821) and bib0041 (J. Mol. Neurosci., 10.1007/s12031-019-01446-1). In the verified primary abstracts, abstract_03 (10.1016/j.jad.2020.07.068) explicitly reports a case-control study of 90 MDD inpatients and 90 matched HCs with significantly lower OXT promoter methylation in MDD vs. HC, plus SLE and depression-severity analyses. By contrast, abstract_04 (10.1007/s12031-019-01446-1) reports N = 146 MDD inpatients examining SLEs, depression severity, and sex differences, with no HC group in its title or abstract. Although the 2024 body/in-text citations and both 2020 full bodies remain inaccessible (so unreported body contrasts in bib0041 are not assumed impossible from title/abstract alone), under Codebook Step 2 only bib0042 positively states the retested MDD-vs.-HC OXT hypomethylation finding; hypothetical unseen body analyses in bib0041 do not make two references fit equally well. Target 0 therefore binds by description to shipped row 821 and is already represented.
